REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - APRIL 12, 2018 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
APRIL 12, 2018, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was led by Pastor Westra from Trinity Christian Reformed
  Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Girl Scout Troop Multilevel Unit Cerritos
  Troop 1043.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations

  Proclamations were presented to:

  Donate Life One Legacy Ambassador Maria Jimenez (DMV/Donate Life
  California Month).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  C.W. Vanderlinden inquired regarding the City's position regarding homeless
  activity in the community.

  G. Satish expressed concern regarding illegal recreational vehicle parking in
  the community.

  James Rivera expressed concern with "sanctuary city" policies enacted by
  Governor Brown and inquired whether the City Council will take a position on
  this matter.

  John Watts expressed concern with accidents at the intersection of 195th
  Street and Albert Avenue in Cerritos. He submitted a document for the record.

  Gail Grossman reminded the audience today is "Holocaust Memorial Day." She
  expressed concern that emails sent to the City Council through the City's
  webpage are not acknowledged.
 City of Cerritos  April 12, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 5

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Rocky Pavone notified the community regarding "Financial Literacy Month" and
  his financial literacy services.

  Murali Vasudevan expressed concern regarding the City Council contact page
  on the City's website, the safety of the City's Easter Egg Hunt, and the City's
  stance on various matters.

  Sam Desai offered gift certificates to the City, expressed concern regarding
  public safety, and that the community’s desires are considered during the
  upcoming budget review.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted
  by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  March 22, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of March 22, 2018
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Register of Demands

  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated April 12,
  2018 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  1. City of Cerritos  4/12/2018  $8,931,885.55  (COUNCIL)
  2. Successor Agency  2/22/2018  $2,160,886.25  (SUCCESSOR AGENCY)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  April 12, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 5

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  Award of Bid No. 1334-18, Supply and  Delivery  70/30  Blend
  Polyorthophosphate in 55 Gallon Drums (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to Award of Bid
  No. 1334-18, Supply and Delivery 70/30 Blend Polyorthophosphate in 55
  Gallon Drums to Carus Corporation in an annual estimated contract value of
  $55,000.00 to $60,000.00 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS ADOPTING AN UPDATED
  ENGINEERING AND TRAFFIC SURVEY IN ACCORDANCE WITH CALIFORNIA
  VEHICLE CODE SECTION 40802 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed the public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to waive
  further reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2018-06, A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS ADOPTING AN
  UPDATED ENGINEERING AND TRAFFICSURVEY IN ACCORDANCE WITH
  CALIFORNIA VEHICLE CODE SECTION 40802 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of a cable television service agreement for City
  facilities (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Laura Kajiwara, Public Information Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed the public comments.
 City of Cerritos  April 12, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve staff to
  enter into an agreement with Spectrum to provide annual cable television services
  to the City of Cerritos in the amount of $17,716.20. The term of the contract would
  cover 12 months from May 2018 to April 2019, with an option to renew by mutual
  agreement of both parties for up to three additional 12-month terms (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS ADOPTING A LIST OF
  PROJECTS TO BE FUNDED BY SENATE BILL 1: ROAD REPAIR AND
  ACCOUNTABILITY ACT FUNDS, FOR FISCAL YEAR 2018-2019 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Finance Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed the public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Pulido, to waive full
  reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2018-05, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS ADOPTING A LIST OF
  PROJECTS TO BE FUNDED BY SENATE BILL 1: ROAD REPAIR AND
  ACCOUNTABILITY ACT FUNDS, FOR FISCAL YEAR 2018-2019
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State
  or Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.
 City of Cerritos  April 12, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 5

10.  Legislative Items (continued)

10B.  (continued)

10B1. Review and consideration of legislation and to oppose Senate Bill 827 (Weiner)
  which proposes to allow the construction of housing developments near major
  transit stops without compliance with local land use regulations (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathleen Jung Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed the public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to oppose SB
  827 (Weiner) and direct staff to prepare a letter of opposition to Senator Scott
  Weiner with copies to the Senate Transportation and Housing Committee and
  Senate Committee on Governance and Finance and the appropriate city
  affiliations.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Yokoyama, Pulido, Solanki,
  Edwards, and Mayor Hu.

12.  Closed Session

  The City Council did not recess to Closed Session and no items on the Closed
  Session agenda were discussed.

12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL).
  Title: City Manager

12B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL).
  Title: City Attorney

12C.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL).
  Title: City Clerk

13.  Adjournment
  The meeting was adjourned at 8:33 p.m. in memory of Manuel “Popsie” Lelin.

  /s/Vida Barone______________________
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary

/s/Mark E. Pulido__________
Mark E. Pulido, Mayor/Chair

APPROVED: April 26, 2018
